# THEORYs with `tags` `self`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Self** — what a self is — the minimal, bodily and pre-reflective self, self-models and the sense of being a subject, the self as process or as context, and whether machines or groups can be selves. Not the person, which is personhood (group: philosophy; ADR-024).

| [THEORY-044](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-044.md) v2 | Self as context is a learned deictic perspective | Barnes-Holmes et al. ([LIT-541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-541.md)) define three selves: the conceptualized self, the content of verbal relations about oneself; the knowing self, their ongoing process; and the transcendent self, their context. Hayes et al. ([LIT-555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-555.md)) say the third arises from deictic frames (I–you, here–there, now–then) as "a sense of self as a locus or perspective", and is "a context for verbal knowing, not the content", so its limits "cannot be consciously known". The account maps the three onto the record's holdings: the content is the narrative self (Dennett, Gallagher, Strawson), and the context is what Hume could not find among his perceptions and what Metzinger calls a transparent perspective. It differs from the minimal self (Gallagher) on origin: RFT says the perspective is learned in language. The evidence for the learned origin is cited, not read, so Proposed. The clinical claim is [THEORY-051](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-051.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-051](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-051.md) v4 | Self as context is how ACT reduces suffering | ACT names the self as context as one of its six processes: from it "one can be aware of ones own flow of experiences without attachment to them", so it fosters defusion and acceptance, and mindfulness exercises and metaphors foster it (Hayes et al., [LIT-555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-555.md)). RFT reads defusion as moving thoughts from I HERE NOW to I THERE THEN, a deictic shift (Barnes-Holmes et al., [LIT-541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-541.md)), labelled "no more than a heuristic". No study in the record tests the self as context as a process. Its only support is borrowed from small defusion studies under RFT's reading, so Proposed on weak grounds. The conceptual account of the self is [THEORY-044](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-044.md). | Proposed |

Active as a statement of what the model says and does not say, all of it in the text. | [THEORY-1570](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1570.md) v2 | Empathic helping is group-level egoism | A conceptual paper answering May's objection to the self–other merging hypothesis, read in full in [NOTE-1277](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1277.md). It sets Batson et al.'s 1997 rebuttal aside as out of scope, and on its constitutive reading empathy always brings identification with it. Filed from [NOTE-1277](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1277.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1572](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1572.md) v2 | We are essentially embodied wills | Johnston (2023), [LIT-1788](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1788.md), read in [NOTE-1257](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1257.md) in place of Surviving Death ([LIT-1759](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1759.md)). The book's surrogate for the resurrection hope, living on "in the onward rush of humankind" as a self fixed by future-directed attitudes, is given up because reductionist selves multiply bearers of moral status. Programmatic: many arguments are deferred to other papers, and theism carries the account of where wills come from. | Active |
| [THEORY-1581](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1581.md) v3 | Self-activation raises fused willingness to die | Five preliminary studies and three two-wave experiments with Spanish students and adults, read in full in [NOTE-1256](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1256.md). Fusion, the self drawn wholly inside the group, is bimodal, related to but distinct from identification and specific to one group. Outcomes are self-reported intentions; nobody fought or died. Filed from [NOTE-1256](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1256.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1583](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1583.md) v2 | Self-definition predicts guilt, investment excuses | Seven studies with Dutch students, read in full in [NOTE-1262](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1262.md). Self-definition (self-stereotyping, in-group homogeneity) and self-investment (solidarity, satisfaction, centrality) correlate .61 to .77 yet predict different reactions; the key guilt test has N = 49. The self–group overlap circles went more with investment than with self-stereotyping. Filed from [NOTE-1262](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1262.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1589](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1589.md) v2 | Only name memorization made implicit in-group bias | Two experiments with US undergraduates (N = 42, 73), read in full in [NOTE-1319](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1319.md), with cells of 13 to 25. The classic painting-preference induction gave no reliable implicit effect; implicit and explicit measures correlated weakly; allocation favouritism tracked explicit identification (r = .37) and was carried mostly by one colour group. Filed from [NOTE-1319](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1319.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1590](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1590.md) v3 | Self is construed independent or interdependent | A theoretical review, read in full in [NOTE-1275](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1275.md), with thin primary evidence: several central studies were unpublished, and nationality stands in for construal. It names "a self defined in relationship to others" as an alternative to selfishness and selflessness, and reads the resulting action as possibly altruistic. Filed from [NOTE-1275](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1275.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1592](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1592.md) v3 | Group identification yields group-based emotion | Smith and Mackie (2016), [LIT-1690](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1690.md), read in [NOTE-1285](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1285.md). A five-page review by the founders of intergroup emotions theory, with no new data. Four facts: the emotion follows the salient membership; members converge on a group norm; no personal involvement is needed; identification moderates, the highly identified sometimes reappraising to avoid guilt. Group-based emotions predict collective action and can be regulated. | Active |
| [THEORY-1595](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1595.md) v2 | Low self-esteem doesn't drive discrimination | A qualitative review of over 40 studies, read in full in [NOTE-1278](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1278.md): 18 experiments for and 13 against the first corollary, 7 for and 28 against the second, with no effect sizes. Only two studies measured esteem for the group itself, and both support the motive. Filed from [NOTE-1278](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1278.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1597](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1597.md) v2 | Ancestral injury becomes a chosen trauma | Volkan (2021), a memorial lecture, read in place of his 2001 paper ([NOTE-1250](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1250.md)). A restatement of large-group psychology, with no method, sample or contrary cases: every observation is the author's. It is the named source of [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md)'s identity route, and its mechanism is parents depositing the identity in children, so on it the identity and parenting routes do not come apart. | Active |
| [THEORY-1603](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1603.md) v2 | People seek positive identity via comparison | A textbook chapter with no new evidence, read in full in [NOTE-1315](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1315.md). It states the needs a positive social identity serves in the individual's terms (certainty, self-esteem, meaning) and reports, without a source, that where identification's components are separated, commitment predicts behaviour better than self-categorization. Filed from [NOTE-1315](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1315.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1609](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1609.md) v2 | Low future-self similarity predicts impatience | Hershfield (2011), [LIT-1702](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1702.md), read in [NOTE-1259](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1259.md) from the accepted manuscript. Following Parfit, future self-continuity has three proposed components, similarity, vividness and positivity, each measured or manipulated in studies of saving and discounting. Apart from one r = .47, the review gives no effect sizes. It suggests, untested, that late in life the future self may continue in one's offspring. | Active |
| [THEORY-1619](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1619.md) v2 | Minimal groups yield favouritism with fairness | A brief review of the minimal group paradigm, read in full in [NOTE-1301](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1301.md), with no figures; most of the self-anchoring work is from the author's circle. It is criticized as reciprocity, as projection, and as limited to positive resources. Filed from [NOTE-1301](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1301.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1624](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1624.md) v2 | Psychological altruism is not yet established | The Stanford Encyclopedia survey, read in full in [NOTE-1274](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1274.md). It reports the 1997 exchange's outcome in one sentence, with no numbers: Batson et al. avoided Cialdini et al.'s methodological problems and found empathy's role "clearly evident". Its argument from numerical identity does not consider an extended self-concept short of identity. Filed from [NOTE-1274](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1274.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1625](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1625.md) v2 | Partners include each other in the self | A short review by Aron's group, with no new data, read in full in [NOTE-1276](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1276.md). Overlap goes with treating a partner's outcomes and standing as one's own, for good and ill. The cognitive signs of inclusion, unlike the scale, concern the processing of one's own self-concept. Filed from [NOTE-1276](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1276.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1631](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1631.md) | Lived immortality modes predict their consolation | Sturesteps (1992), [LIT-1689](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1689.md), an ANU master's thesis skimmed in [NOTE-1312](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1312.md) in place of Lifton (1979, [LIT-1714](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1714.md)). It tests Rank's three modes and Lifton's two added ones with vignettes rated as consolation, separating having a mode (availability) from accepting it. Cross-sectional; Rank's sex-difference and neuroticism hypotheses failed. The copy limits copying, so almost nothing is quoted. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1632](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1632.md) v2 | Relational and collective selves serve two needs | A draft chapter, read in full in [NOTE-1290](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1290.md). Group and interpersonal attachment correlate only .46 (anxiety) and .33 (avoidance), and loneliness has relational and collective factors. Relational collectivism, obligation to particular persons, is set apart from group-based collectivism. Filed from [NOTE-1290](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1290.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1677](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1677.md) | Recommenders both erode and aid authenticity | Étienne Brown, read in [NOTE-1792](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1792.md) (Read). Brown argues that recommender systems affect users' capacity to be their authentic selves, both negatively and positively. He offers a "minimal", multi-dimensional account of authenticity with two dimensions: volitional alignment (Frankfurt, via Rings: acting on first-order desires one reflectively endorses at second order) and self-understanding (an epistemic dimension, relational rather than purely introspective: others' testimony and recommendations are a source of self-knowledge). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2126](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2126.md) | Egocentrism is self–other undifferentiation | From the reading of [LIT-2892](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2892.md) in [NOTE-2208](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2208.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2212.md) | Expected group continuity lowers prejudice | Simić, Sacchi and Perugini (2025), three Italian studies, the third a preregistered experiment (N = 252), read in full ([NOTE-2302](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2302.md)). The continuity is the group's with its own future, measured with future-self-continuity items; it correlated .14 with national attachment. The effects on prejudice and collective action needed a covariate outside the preregistration, and the moderation by attachment came from an analysis that left it. Nothing here concerns future people or legacy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2225](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2225.md) | Future-self link to posterity is correlational | Syropoulos, Law, Coleman and Young, read in [NOTE-2315](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2315.md) (Read), from the 2024-05-21 manuscript. Self-oriented prospection correlates with responsibility for future generations across studies; mediation through identification is cross-sectional; and the two pre-registered experiments give a small effect on responsibility and then a null, with no effect on identification. The identification measure includes empathy and perspective-taking. | Proposed |
